  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R36"],
      "pins": ["R36.1", "R36.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R36 is labelled 24k, but its description and LCSC/MPN identify a 24Ω part (FRC0805J240TSD, 0805, 125mW, 150V). It sits directly across the high-voltage rails VOUTP and VOUTN.",
      "expected": "A 24 kΩ resistor in this high-voltage position, consistent with the value field, or a 24Ω part whose label and metadata agree with it.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R36\") (value \"24k\") ... (description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R36 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the part is really 24Ω, it would conduct about 100V/24Ω ≈ 4 A across the high-voltage rail, far beyond its 125 mW rating, and would overheat or fail. The bleed or divider function would also be lost. The value and part are inconsistent.",
      "confidence": 0.7
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D30", "R60", "R59"],
      "pins": ["D30.4", "D30.2", "R60.2", "R59.2"],
      "nets": ["ESTOP_OUT", "Net-(D30-K2)", "Net-(D30-K1)"],
      "observed": "The second LED channel of dual LED D30 has its anode (A2, pin 4) on ESTOP_OUT and its cathode (K2, pin 2) connected through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. The matching channel K1 uses R59 to GND. The LED therefore has no voltage across it and cannot light.",
      "expected": "The resistor on the K2 cathode should return to GND, as R59 does for K1, so that the ESTOP_OUT indicator can conduct when the line is driven.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"67\") (name \"ESTOP_OUT\") ... (node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") ...) (node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"2\") ...)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"129\") (name \"Net-(D30-K2)\") ... (node (ref \"R60\") (pin \"1\") ...)"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R60 Net-_D30-K2_ ESTOP_OUT 130"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R59 Net-_D30-K1_ 0 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "The E-stop status indicator channel never lights, so the operator gets no visual confirmation of the ESTOP_OUT state. Otherwise the circuit is functionally unchanged.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "polarity",
      "components": ["Q1", "U6"],
      "pins": ["Q1.2", "Q1.3", "U6.1", "U6.6"],
      "nets": ["USBC_VBUS_IN", "+5V"],
      "observed": "The LTC4412 ideal-diode PMOS Q1 has its source (pin 2) on +5V, which is also the LTC4412 SENSE node (U6.6). Its drain (pin 3) is on USBC_VBUS_IN, which is the controller VIN input. The body diode therefore conducts from +5V back toward the USB input.",
      "expected": "For an input-to-output ideal-diode OR-ing path, the PMOS source should be on the input (VIN/USBC_VBUS_IN) and the drain on the output, with SENSE on the output. The body diode should then block reverse current from the load.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"2\") (name \"+5V\") ... (node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") ...)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"207\") (name \"USBC_VBUS_IN\") ... (node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") ...) (node (ref \"U6\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"VIN\") ...)"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "USB input \"OR-ing\"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, U6)"}
      ],
      "impact": "Reverse-current protection, the stated purpose of the ideal-diode arrangement, may not work as intended. Power could back-feed onto the USB input, or the USB path could be blocked in the wrong direction.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The strongest finding is R36, whose 24k value conflicts with its 24Ω part metadata and would overheat across the high-voltage rail. Two lower-confidence possibilities are the E-stop LED channel of D30 being shorted by R60, and the LTC4412 PMOS Q1 having source and drain arranged in reverse."
}

anomalies.expected: For an input-to-output ideal-diode OR-ing path, the PMOS source should be on the input (VIN/USBC_VBUS_IN) and the drain on the output, with SENSE on the output. The body diode should then block reverse current from the load.
